note: 20 original meme concepts. All reuse_status=original: our own words, drawn in Pillow or set on a CC0/licensed object photo with no people. Numbers in jokes are deliberately silly personal numbers, never presented as research. Scores are 1-5 and only order the review; they never override a gate.

concepts.punch: is now load-bearing.
concepts.visual: Typographic card. Optional photo version: a stack of books propping up a wobbly table leg (CC0 object photo, no people).
concepts.caption: It's holding up the shelf. Emotionally, it's holding up me.
concepts.format: Single image (or 2-slide carousel: joke, then photo)
concepts.why: Books pillar, instantly recognisable, sendable to any reader friend. No lesson needed.
concepts.concerns: None. Photo must show only objects.

bars: Nights I went to bed on time
concepts.punch: My numbers. Not science.
concepts.visual: Two horizontal bars, Bone and Ember, on Slate. Small label: 'My numbers. Not science.'
concepts.caption: Currently listening to number 48. In bed. At 1am.
concepts.why: The gap between knowing and doing is the page's core idea, shown as a joke instead of a lecture.
concepts.concerns: Numbers are obviously personal and labelled 'not science', so they can't be read as a stat.
concepts.footnote: Epictetus spent whole lectures on this gap: knowing the rule is not the same as living it.

concepts.setup: Finally finished a book about attention.
concepts.punch: Well. The introduction. And four notifications.
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: Chapter one is going really well though.
concepts.why: Attention and digital life, self-aware, no product named.
concepts.concerns: Don't name a real book: avoids implying we read or reviewed it.

concepts.punch: You already have.
concepts.visual: Flowchart: three question boxes, every arrow (yes or no) leads to one box: 'You already have.'
concepts.caption: Flowchart completed in 0.4 seconds.
concepts.why: Clever visual joke that works with no explanation. Highly shareable.
concepts.concerns: Use a generic phone, never a brand logo or real app UI.

concepts.setup: Marcus Aurelius wrote his notebook while running an empire.
concepts.punch: I can't finish a shopping list while the kettle boils.
concepts.visual: Typographic card. No statues or busts (brand rule).
concepts.caption: In fairness, he didn't have to remember oat milk.
concepts.why: Philosophy applied to an ordinary moment; the joke is on us, not on Marcus.
concepts.concerns: Fact check: the Meditations were private notes written while he was emperor (parts on campaign). 'Notebook' keeps it accurate without a quote.

concepts.setup: Seneca's whole argument: life is long if you know how to use it.
concepts.punch: Me, 40 minutes into choosing what to watch:
concepts.visual: Two-panel: top panel the line; bottom panel a plain glowing rectangle (a 'screen') with a scroll bar, no real streaming UI.
concepts.caption: Watched the trailer for three things. Went to bed.
concepts.why: Smuggles a real idea (On the Shortness of Life) into a universal habit.
concepts.concerns: Paraphrase, not a quote: keep the words 'whole argument' so it reads as a summary. No streaming-service branding.
concepts.footnote: Paraphrase of Seneca, On the Shortness of Life, ch. 1.

concepts.setup: Wrote three pages in my journal about being present.
concepts.punch: Checked my phone between each one.
concepts.visual: Typographic card. Optional photo: an open notebook with a phone face-down on it (no people).
concepts.caption: Page four will be about acceptance.
concepts.why: Ties to the journal product without selling anything.
concepts.concerns: Never place a journal promo inside this meme (keeps memes and commercial posts separate).

concepts.setup: My motivation, by time of day
concepts.punch: The motivation arrives. The day has left.
concepts.visual: Flat line all day, then a spike at 11:58pm labelled 'Suddenly ready to reorganise my whole life'.
concepts.caption: Tomorrow's plan was written at 11:59pm. Tomorrow's me has notes.
concepts.why: Procrastination was our best-performing theme in reels; a chart makes it visual and shareable.
concepts.concerns: None.

concepts.punch: Spent nine of them planning lunch.
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: The tenth minute was very peaceful. It was about soup.
concepts.why: Gentle spirituality humour that laughs at the practitioner, never the practice.
concepts.concerns: Keep tradition-neutral; no religious imagery.

concepts.punch: Day 2: the shaker is doing great.
concepts.visual: Typographic card. Optional photo: an unused shaker bottle on a kitchen counter (no people, no brand).
concepts.caption: Week 3: the shaker has a gym membership. I visit it.
concepts.why: Gym habits and unrealistic expectations, laughing at ourselves, no body talk.
concepts.concerns: No supplement brand visible (would read as an ad).

concepts.punch: Consistency looks boring from the inside.
concepts.visual: Two lines: 'Expected' a straight diagonal; 'Actual' a wobbly line with labelled dips: 'had a cold', 'Christmas', 'remembered'. Ends slightly higher than it started.
concepts.caption: Still higher than where it started. That counts.
concepts.why: Warm and encouraging without a pep talk; strong save candidate.
concepts.concerns: Avoid weight or body-shape labels on the axis. Axis just says 'Progress'.

concepts.punch: Also yesterday. I am extremely well rested.
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: Recovery is part of the programme. I am recovering from the programme.
concepts.why: Simply funny. Body pillar needs lighter posts.
concepts.concerns: None.

concepts.setup: Films: a whole life transformation in a two-minute montage with great music.
concepts.punch: Me: year three. No music. Still on the stairs.
concepts.visual: Typographic card with a thin 'progress bar' at 2% under the punchline. No film stills or music (rights).
concepts.caption: Somebody please cue the soundtrack.
concepts.why: Film lessons pillar; the gap between story time and real time.
concepts.concerns: No named film, no stills, no score: avoids copyright and implies no endorsement.

concepts.punch: and meaning it on the second draft.
concepts.visual: Typographic card. First draft shown struck through: 'fine.'
concepts.caption: Draft one is between me and God.
concepts.why: Emotional maturity shown honestly: the feeling is real, the reply is chosen.
concepts.concerns: 'Between me and God' is a common idiom, not religious mockery. Swap to 'between me and my drafts folder' if he prefers zero religious reference.

venn: Friends who check how I'm doing
concepts.punch: Same circle.
concepts.visual: Venn diagram where the two circles overlap completely. Label in the middle: 'Same circle.'
concepts.caption: It was always the memes.
concepts.why: Warm, true, and the most natural DM-send in the batch. The send is the point, so no CTA needed.
concepts.concerns: None.

concepts.setup: Rehearsed the difficult conversation in the shower 14 times.
concepts.punch: Real version: 40 seconds. They said 'oh, fair enough.'
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: I had a closing argument. I had rebuttals. I had a backup closing argument.
concepts.format: Single image (or reel: text over CC0 shower-tile footage, no people)
concepts.why: Our best organic theme (the 2am replay carousel, 499 reach) as a joke instead of advice.
concepts.concerns: None.
concepts.footnote: Seneca, Letters 13.4: we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.

concepts.punch: except one text that just says 'ok'.
concepts.visual: Generic message bubble reading 'ok' (no app branding), above the line.
concepts.caption: Not 'okay'. Not 'ok!'. Just 'ok'. Spent the afternoon on it.
concepts.why: Universal, affectionate, no target. Stoicism applied to the smallest possible problem.
concepts.concerns: Bubble must not copy iMessage/WhatsApp design or colours.

concepts.punch: Felt like a saint for the next six miles.
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: Small good thing of the day. Possibly the week.
concepts.why: Kindness pillar with a wink at our own vanity; fits 'Small Good Thing' series.
concepts.concerns: UK spelling and miles: audience is 86% UK.

concepts.setup: Adult friendship is saying 'we must catch up!'
concepts.punch: every four months, forever, with total sincerity.
concepts.visual: Typographic card.
concepts.caption: Love you. See you in February. Possibly.
concepts.why: Very sendable; the send itself is the catch-up.
concepts.concerns: None.

concepts.setup: Things I worried about this year
concepts.punch: My numbers. Not science.
concepts.visual: Three bars. Small label: 'My numbers. Not science.'
concepts.caption: Already worried about next year's chart.
concepts.format: Single image (or 2-slide carousel with the Seneca footnote)
concepts.why: Seneca's point about imagined suffering, said with a chart instead of a sermon.
concepts.concerns: Anxiety topic: keep it light and personal, no claim that worry is pointless or that this treats anxiety.
concepts.footnote: Seneca, Letters 13.4 (Gummere): 'We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.'
